title: Geopolitical Daily
email_subject: A Russian warship burns in Benghazi
preheader: Zelensky confirms the attack; COP31 ends with no deal; Democrats win 258 seats.
intro_text: Good morning. It's Monday, November 23, 2026 — the 3 stories that matter most today, plus 2 updates on stories you're following and 4 quick items from around the world.

stories.story_title: Ukraine's sea drones hit Russian warship at Libyan base
stories.why_important: Ukrainian sea drones hit the Russian corvette Merkury at Benghazi in eastern Libya. The attack badly damaged the ship and set the base on fire. Zelensky confirmed the attack and said it also hit a cargo ship carrying weapons. Ukraine has now taken its war against Russia's fleet into the Mediterranean.
stories.what_overlooked: Libyan officials say the drones launched from a Ukrainian-run base in western Libya. That unconfirmed claim could pull Libya's divided factions deeper into the war.
stories.prediction: Russia's reply in days will show if Moscow treats Libya as a new front. It could mean strikes on Ukrainian ports or a UN complaint.

stories.story_title: UN climate talks collapse after EU rejects final deal
stories.why_important: The COP31 talks in Antalya ended Sunday with no final agreement at all. The EU and other countries rejected a text from hosts Turkey and Australia. They said it was too weak on fossil fuels and on money for adaptation. The 30-year UN process now faces open doubt.
stories.what_overlooked: Negotiators from the countries most at risk openly asked whether these yearly summits can still deliver, Reuters reported. Doubt now comes from inside the process, not just from its critics.
stories.prediction: Whether Turkey and Australia call a resumed session before year end will show if the UN process can still deliver any deal.

stories.story_title: Democrats win biggest House majority since 1992
stories.why_important: Democrats will hold at least 258 House seats, their largest majority in more than three decades. Leaders say they will use committee power to investigate the Trump administration, from corruption claims to how agencies are run.
stories.what_overlooked: One North Carolina race, Chuck Hubbard's win over Republican Virginia Foxx, pushed the party to 258 seats. That win decides how easily Democrats can force people to testify.
stories.prediction: First subpoena threats from incoming committee chairs in the coming days will show if investigations start before Democrats take power in January.

quick_hits.text: Drones struck Khartoum homes and a UN building; Sudan's army blamed Ethiopia, and the UN said exposing aid workers to such danger is unacceptable.
Congo's foreign minister warned EU countries that sending deported migrants to Rwanda could fund armed militia, saying Brussels is 'looking the other way'.
US intelligence chief Jay Clayton called it 'entirely appropriate' for Trump to call Putin a friend, while saying Putin is 'not America's friend in Ukraine'.
Rescue workers in Dymer, north of Kyiv, recovered 11 bodies from a Russian drone strike that partly collapsed a five-story apartment building.

big_number.context: At least 24 people died when fire tore through a candy factory in Banten, Indonesia; about 30 workers are still missing.

views.framing: Reports Zelensky’s confirmation that Ukraine’s military attacked a Russian corvette off Libya, stressing official Ukrainian responsibility.
views.quote: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has confirmed that Ukraine’s military attacked the Russian Navy corvette Merkury off the coast of Libya.

views.framing: Stresses Ukraine’s successful strike and Russian losses, citing Zelensky and media reports of a destroyed warship.
views.quote: A vessel, believed to be the Russian corvette Merkury, which had been docked for several days at the port of Benghazi in Libya, was destroyed in an explosion.
